title: Explicit Candidate Retention And Recovery
summary: P3C separates historical preparation results from durable cleanup intents, verifies bounded owned file inventories and releases quota only after confirmed filesystem deletion.
personalScopedExtension: Dev58 adds native-only owner cancellation and retention under current WorkspaceWriteScope; see shin-workspace-ownership-v1 internalScopedCleanup. It permits cleanup, not reuse, of obsolete owned jobs. The legacy HTTP API below remains unchanged and enrolled users stay fenced. No automatic scheduler is added.

api.GET /api/v1/preparations/{id}/retention: Authenticated scoped read-only plan/status. No query parameters. Missing and denied jobs both return 404 before filesystem access. Readers may inspect their project but can_apply is false for them.
api.POST /api/v1/preparations/{id}/retention: Administrator-only, exact body {expected_plan_id: 64 lowercase hex characters}. This plan identity scoped to the job is the idempotency token; no separate random Idempotency-Key is required. No client filesystem paths or arbitrary inventory are accepted.
api.envelope: Normal shin.server-response.v1 contains shin.candidate-retention.v1: job_id, state, plan_id, can_apply, reservation_held, artifact_bytes, entries, reason_codes, mutation_performed and automatic_execution=false.
api.authorization: Plan token is a content comparison, not authorization. Any currently authorized administrator may explicitly continue the same persisted plan. Audit preserves both the original requester and the completing principal.
api.admission: One retention operation per server process with nonblocking admission. A busy slot returns 503/retention-busy. Filesystem lifetime locks also exclude competing processes and candidate inspections.
api.errors: Wrong/stale plan returns 409; an existing intent or released record with another plan_id returns retention-plan-conflict. Active jobs, unsafe trees, missing claimed-writer locks and unbound namespaces fail closed. No raw source, inventory paths, artifact key or credentials in public output.

stateModel.preparation: Existing queued/running/prepared/failed/cancelled history and public job JSON are unchanged by retention. prepared remains a historical result, not a claim that its artifact still exists.
stateModel.retention: Absence of a retention row means retained. A committed intent owns one exact cleanup inventory and prevents activation. released means filesystem deletion and directory synchronization were confirmed before the release transaction was committed.
stateModel.activeGeneration: A preparation referenced by an active route cannot be planned or applied for retention. Explicit deactivation removes that reference in the activation transaction; admitted retrieval retains a shared candidate lock until it finishes, so cleanup still cannot race that reader.
stateModel.inspection: Candidate inspection returns candidate-retention-pending or candidate-released before accessing artifacts; it does not reuse a historical prepared result as current evidence.
stateModel.releasedObservation: GET and replay of released state read the durable ledger only. They do not re-inspect disk and do not prove that an uncooperative external process has not subsequently created new files.
stateModel.recovery: Restart never auto-applies an intent. GET reports intent and reservation_held=true; an administrator repeats POST with the same plan_id. Already removed entries are permitted only after a durable intent, while remaining entries must match that inventory.

artifactIdentity.namespace: SHA256 over shin.artifact-namespace.v1, canonical private state root and its device/inode identity. Separate from route, profile, Core version and generation-limit fingerprints; source drift does not prevent cleanup of owned cache data.
artifactIdentity.key: Each new preparation receives a unique random 256-bit artifact_key from OpenSSL RAND_bytes. Store invokes its factory only after replay and admission checks, so an existing idempotency record does not depend on fresh entropy. The key is not part of the stable enqueue request hash.
artifactIdentity.layout: state_dir/job-<id>-<artifact_key> and the permanent empty mode-0600 .job-<id>-<artifact_key>.lock. Nonces prevent a reused DB id from referring to another artifact after a controlled database reset.
artifactIdentity.migration: Explicit migration 003 adds paired nullable namespace/key columns and preparation_retention. Existing development rows remain unbound rather than receiving guessed filesystem authority. No compatibility reader or automatic backfill. Old unbound artifacts require separate operator inventory; they are not silently deleted or released.
artifactIdentity.lifetime: Claimed jobs allocate their exclusive lifetime fence before route/source work. Cleanup needs an exclusive existing fence even for an expired DB state. A missing claimed-writer lock is not proof of quiescence.
artifactIdentity.neverClaimed: A cancelled job with worker_id=null and no artifact may be planned without creating a lock. Only an explicit valid POST may allocate its permanent empty fence before recording intent. This is not a read-path repair.

deletionProtocol: Authorize the job, require terminal state and matching namespace, verify private state identity and acquire the nonblocking exclusive lifetime lock.

Capture only the fixed Core generated-file/control-file layout and its known directories. Recognized partial or corrupt cache data can be removed; unknown entries, symlinks, hard links, special files and oversized inventories cannot.
Bind the plan to the historical job, namespace/key, exact entry names/types, inode identities, modes, byte counts and streaming SHA256 file hashes. GET never publishes this private inventory.
Commit the intent and correlated audit event in PostgreSQL before destructive IO. If commit acknowledgement is uncertain, return failure without guessing rollback or deleting files.

Confirm the remaining tree is a matching subset of the durable inventory. Remove only those entries bottom-up via openat/fstatat/unlinkat with no-follow directory descriptors. Do not use recursive remove_all on managed product state.
Synchronize each modified parent directory and the pinned state root, confirm the candidate path is absent, then atomically mark released and append one release audit event.
Keep the lifetime lock inode, job record, original reservation value and idempotency history. Repeated completed requests are read-only and do not add audit events or regenerate artifacts.

limits.diskReservation: Count and summed reserved bytes exclude only released jobs. Intent, failure, cancellation, unknown or unbound states continue holding quota. The existing global reservation ceiling remains 1 GiB.
limits.history: Independent hard cap of 65536 preparation records bounds retained metadata, idempotency tombstones and permanent fence count. At capacity reject new requests with preparation-history-capacity, but still allow existing idempotent replays. Automatic history pruning is not implemented.
limits.inventory: At most 64 ledger entries and 32768 encoded bytes; the filesystem additionally restricts entries to the smaller fixed managed layout. Total file content cannot exceed that job's reserved bytes. SHA256 is streamed through a 64 KiB buffer, not loaded as one full generation.
limits.execution: One bounded scan/cleanup at a time. Filesystem calls and fsync retain operating-system wait semantics; this is not a hard deadline or a total RSS guarantee.

boundaries.ownership: Private server-owned candidate artifacts only, never active route output, consumer source or an arbitrary directory supplied by a client. External Core publishers must not write into this private namespace; it is not a generic index-prune API.
boundaries.security: Local filesystem and cooperating same-host actors. Advisory locks are not a sandbox against malicious or uncooperative same-UID file writers. Missing/replaced fence identity fails closed. NFS/SMB and distributed/HA deletion are not certified.
boundaries.remaining: Unknown staging files/orphans and old unbound artifacts are refused, not swept automatically. History lifecycle, power-loss durability certification and hard worker deadlines remain separate work.
boundaries.activation: P3D2 makes the active-generation pointer a DB-only route reference. Retention neither creates nor changes it; activation rejects an existing retention intent. Current verification is recorded in shin-server-activation-evidence-v1.

sources.use: CHECK also accepts unknown/null; paired identity constraints must explicitly require both populated values.
Descriptor-relative unlinkat and empty-directory removal; open descriptors are not erased by unlink.
Filesystem data and parent-directory durability require explicit synchronization; DB commit is separate.
